source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text:
Harvest timing: the manual explains that harvest should happen once pods have reached full mature color (R8 stage — 95% of pods brown) but before pods over-dry and begin to shatter in the field, which can cause serious yield loss especially with mechanical harvesting or in windy/rainy conditions at maturity. Manual (sickle/hand-pulling) and mechanized (combine) harvest methods are both covered, with a photo showing both a combine harvester and hand-cut windrows drying in the field.

Post-cut handling: cut plants are windrowed and field-dried before threshing if not combine-harvested directly; the manual gives guidance on drying floor/tarpaulin threshing and moisture-content targets before storage (~13–14% moisture cited as a safe storage target), and recommends prompt threshing after cutting to minimize field losses from shattering, pests, and weather.
